synth.twoLeverPath:
TWO LEVERS to strictly sub-native (df631112 OPT-1 + OPT-A; both LOSSLESS-by-construction, tree-only/align-to-native per 6c5aeaae). STALENESS CORRECTION (resolved, committed 16fdb982): the lm-head lineage read called both "UNBUILT" — WRONG. Direct git inspection confirms both are IMPLEMENTED first-drafts on main HEAD: OPT-1 = 10ebccac (merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD = True), OPT-A = e90de7ef (ancestor = True), each introduced by its named commit (git log -S on both patch fns), both default-OFF, both with passing CPU byte-A/B gates, NEITHER GPU-verified. They are NOT exported in fr13_launch_locked.sh (= not engaged in the deployed 0.2248 build, consistent with implemented-but-unverified).

OPT-1 = GPU-RESIDENT COMMITTER (10ebccac, FR13_GPU_COMMITTER). REACH: removes the dominant remaining main-thread tax = the committer's packed DtoH+sync (the surviving wait location after FIX-2 collapsed 6 DtoH -> 1; main thread blocked 91.9% vs native 0.8%). INFERRED reclaim ~4-6 ms of the ~6.5 ms tax -> s/fwd parity-to-just-below native; chain5 (+4.4 ms) crosses below native FIRST; the WIN is the accept-edge becoming a TPS win at s/fwd parity (cat9 ~3.18 vs native ~3.07 tok/fwd), NOT a large s/fwd gain. STATUS: implemented first-draft (CPU byte-A/B 52/52 trees byte-identical, accept/path-LCP decision verified pure-integer at fr10_phase4...:5780-5879), NOT GPU-verified. LOSSLESS=STRONG (pure-integer, location-only host->Triton move, a0e8cc3d holds=True; flag-off path byte-identical). TREE-ONLY=CLEAN (flag-guarded branch, touches the tree committer only). BLOCKER: G2 "kill the sync" (side-stream the readback + CUDA event) is the ACTUAL win and is UNBUILT — the first draft still does a host .cpu().tolist() readback. Needs GPU boot, large effort.

OPT-A = GB10-TUNED fp8 GEMV CONFIG (e90de7ef, FR13_GB10_FP8_GEMV_CFG). REACH: attacks native's OWN ~45%-of-peak bandwidth slack (native pays the same 85 ms/draft fp8 lm-head = 39% of its forward), so it is a sub-native lever for BOTH arms. INFERRED ~140-150 ms/fwd = ~1.45-1.55x vs native 218 ms — a FUNDAMENTAL bandwidth win, NOT the 98.6 ms BW floor (26.9 GB / 273 GB/s; GB10 lacks TMA/WGMMA/cp.async.bulk). VERIFIED vs live fp8_utils.py (pinned 3dbe092e): no GB10/sm_121 config -> get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs returns None -> default BLOCK_SIZE_M=64/GROUP_SIZE_M=32/num_warps=4/num_stages=2; K-accum (fp32 accumulator, acc += tl.dot*a_s*b_s) is K-order-independent of M-tiling when BLOCK_SIZE_K=128 pinned -> bit-identical output. STATUS: implemented first-draft (CPU byte-A/B G0-G3 pass), NOT GPU-verified. LOSSLESS=STRONG (BLOCK_SIZE_K=128 pinned -> fp32 K-accum order unchanged, bit-identical bytes; HARD-EXCLUDE Split-K/RevSplit-K). TREE-ONLY=TENSION/FLAG-FOR-USER: it patches w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm, a SHARED kernel native also runs, and the M<=32 guard catches native MTP-5 decode too — strictly a shared-path config tune, "deviate-shared"-adjacent under 6c5aeaae. Defense: output is bit-identical (align-to-native in output, scheduling-only). NEEDS a user ruling on whether shared-but-bit-exact config tuning is in-scope.

COMBINED PATH: cat9 already has a tiny REAL accept edge (+0.0176, per-event superset net +15 lossless leaf-saves over E5 with 0 spine-regressions). Neither axis alone reliably clears (break-even = accept ~3.43 at 1.05x s/fwd). But OPT-1 (s/fwd 1.030x -> ~parity, turning the accept edge into a TPS win) AND/OR OPT-A (s/fwd -> ~1.45-1.55x, fundamental for both arms) each independently project STRICTLY sub-native, and together comfortably. A cheap numerator lever (L3 confidence-gated root sibling, free-to-gate, +0.035 MEASURED to +0.08-0.15 INFERRED, NOT on HEAD) further widens the margin. ALL per-forward ms are INFERRED — the clean GPU measurement is the arbiter.

synth.subNativeVerdict:
YES — strictly sub-native B=1 TPS is reachable via OPT-1 + OPT-A, confirming the user's "very close + two levers" call with the corrected numbers (NOT the stale 2.3x). The current state is the foundation: cat9 ~1.030x native s/fwd (+6.5 ms) at accept-PARITY-to-EDGE (3.18 >= 3.161, +0.0176; per-event superset net +15 lossless, 0 spine-regressions) and lossless-at-scale (13.55% ~= 13.99%). So the numerator is already not the blocker — the verdict is gated entirely by the s/fwd denominator, and each lever reaches it:
- OPT-A alone (INFERRED ~1.45-1.55x s/fwd / 140-150 ms vs 218) over-clears strictly-sub-native by a wide margin (fundamental bandwidth win attacking native's own 45%-of-peak slack, bit-identical output).
- OPT-1 alone (INFERRED ~4-6 ms reclaim) brings s/fwd to ~parity-to-just-below native, at which point the existing accept edge makes cat9 a strict TPS win (chain5 crosses on s/fwd first).
- Combined they over-deliver; the cheap L3 accept lever (+0.035 to +0.08-0.15, not on HEAD) is the margin insurance.

ORDER TO APPLY: (1) OPT-1 FIRST — it is the dominant CURRENT tax (committer DtoH+sync, 91.9% main-thread block), tree-only-CLEAN (no scope tension), pure-integer lossless (STRONG), and validates the run-ahead restoration cheaply; build the G2 sync-kill (side-stream readback + CUDA event), which is the unbuilt actual win. (2) OPT-A SECOND — larger reach but carries the shared-kernel scope TENSION (patches w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm that native also runs; M<=32 guard catches native MTP-5 decode) so it needs a USER RULING on whether shared-but-bit-exact config tuning is in-scope before it ships, even though it is lossless-by-construction (BLOCK_SIZE_K=128 pinned, K-accum unchanged). COMPLIANCE: both are tree-only/align-to-native (6c5aeaae) — OPT-1 cleanly, OPT-A via bit-identical output (scheduling-only, flagged for the user). Lossless held as the per-change gate (byte-A/B + per-token argmax + same-seed greedy byte-identical streams + accept/event unchanged) for both.
